_doc: #777 FLEET ALERTS policy, read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-alerts-guard.py (fleet-alerts-guard.yml, every push). Every fleet app raises its user-facing alerts through ONE API, libs:core FleetAlerts, so they land in the SuperApp's Alerts group (G4 of Configs > Launcher > Notify) instead of a channel of their own. The guard fails when any source file in an app or lib tree calls NotificationManager(.Compat).notify(...) without being listed in `posters` below with a `kind` from `kinds` — i.e. a new direct notification must be classified (a badge, a foreground service, media, a user action, the app's own messages...) or go through FleetAlerts. It also fails when a listed file's notify() call count changes (a new alert slipped into an exempt file), when a listed file no longer exists or no longer posts (a stale exemption hides nothing but reads as policy), and when a kind is not in the vocabulary — there is deliberately no `alert` kind. Adding an exemption is a DATA edit here, with its reason.
_rule: an alert goes through FleetAlerts (libs:core); a direct notify() is only for what is not an alert, and says what it is.
_doc_prune_dirs: Generated output, third-party modules, retired trees and TEST source sets (tests post notifications to assert on them).
_doc_notify_call: A NotificationManager/NotificationManagerCompat post. Object.notify() (no arguments) is excluded by requiring an argument; comments are stripped before matching, so a note that names notify() is not a call.

kinds.badge: a persistent badge of one of the four shade groups, re-posted by its owner
kinds.media: a media transport mirroring a playback session
kinds.group_summary: the summary of a shade group
kinds.fleet_alerts: the FleetAlerts API itself: the collector's Alerts group or the API's local fallback
kinds.user_action: a prompt wrapping a system Intent the user must act on (PendingIntent payload a deep link cannot carry)
kinds.foreground_service: the ongoing notification a foreground service must hold
kinds.ongoing_controls: an ongoing notification whose content is live controls, or the app's own user-set reminder
kinds.domain_messages: the app's own content (mail, chat, vault requests) — the user's messages, not alerts about the fleet
kinds.upstream_fork: an alert in vendored upstream code that cannot be expressed as a FleetAlert today; the reason says why
kinds.not_a_notification: a method named notify() that is not an Android notification

posters.why: Wireless-debugging pairing (Shizuku's flow): the foreground service's code-entry notification (a RemoteInput the user types the pairing code into, which a deep link cannot carry) and its dismissible pass/fail result. Not an alert about the fleet.
G1 Health badge: a foreground service re-posting its own live readout.
#812 Store badge (Notify > Store): the pending-updates count, non-persistent, cleared at 0 or when the Store opens. A count, not an alert.
G5 Data badge (Network group): a foreground service re-posting data usage (today, month, top apps) when the screen comes on or on Refresh.
G5 Network badge: a foreground service re-posting the mesh state (connection, IP, peers, traffic), event-driven plus a 30s tick while connected.
Battery badge: a foreground service re-posting the battery state (time to full or empty, level, current, health), driven by ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED, no timer.
G1 Markets badge: a foreground service re-posting live quotes.
G1 Weather badge: a foreground service re-posting today's forecast.
G2 KDE Connect badge: a foreground service re-posting the paired desktop's state.
G2 Quick Actions badge: the floating button host's foreground notification (bare re-post + swipe re-post).
G3 Media Player badge: the transport mirroring the active media session (playing + idle faces).
The summary notification of each of the four shade groups.
THE Alerts group: one child per alert + its summary. Everything raised through FleetAlerts ends here.
The API's own fallback: the raising app's notification when no SuperApp can take the alert.

"Tap to finish installing": wraps the system installer's confirm Intent (a PendingIntent the fleet alert link cannot carry), and #588 needs to know whether THIS notification is visible. The install RESULTS go through FleetAlerts.
Same as the updater lib: the confirm-install prompt wraps the system confirm Intent. Results go through FleetAlerts.
GPS tracking foreground service updating its own ongoing status line.
Running timers with pause/+1 min/reset controls, and the bedtime reminder the user set — the clock app's own product, like a ringing alarm, not a fleet alert.
Ongoing indexing progress bar (setOngoing(true)). The backup FAILURE goes through FleetAlerts.
New mail: per-message notifications with reply/archive actions and an account summary — the user's mail, not an alert about the fleet.
Upstream Mattermost: inline-reply update of a chat message notification.
Upstream Element X: Matrix room messages.
Upstream Element X: incoming/ongoing call notification (full-screen intent, call style).
`pushGatewayApi.notify(...)` is an HTTP call to the Matrix push gateway, not an Android notification.
Upstream Fossify Phone: the ongoing/incoming call notification.
Upstream Bitwarden: a login-approval request that must be answered inside the vault.
Upstream Termux: the session-host foreground service updating its own ongoing notification.
Upstream Termux (nix-on-droid fork): the session-host foreground service.

NOT MIGRATED (#777): upstream Termux crash report. Its tap carries a PendingIntent to ReportActivity with the crash text as extras, which a FleetAlerts string deep link cannot carry, and the file is vendored upstream code kept rebasable.
NOT MIGRATED (#777): upstream Termux plugin-error report, same PendingIntent-with-payload shape as CrashUtils.
NOT MIGRATED (#777): upstream termux-shared crash report (nix-on-droid), same shape as cloud-termux CrashUtils.
NOT MIGRATED (#777): upstream termux-shared plugin-error report (nix-on-droid).

#903 the dataSync foreground service a running Store batch holds: re-posts its own ongoing notification with the Store bar's progress line (StoreStages.progress().text), throttled to once a second. The batch's RESULTS go through FleetAlerts.
